'''Ichikishima Shrine''' (市杵島神社) or '''Ichikishima-hime Shrine''' (市杵島姫神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}}

dedicated to {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵島姫神}}, one of the {{ill|Munakata Three Goddesses|ja|宗像三女神|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|1=Three Munakata Goddesses|qq=Three Munakata Goddesses|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Munakata Three Goddesses|13=User:Immanuelle/Three Munakata Goddesses}}. Due to the syncretism of {{ill|Buddhism|en|Buddhism|qid=Q748|lt=Buddhism}} and [[Shinto]] ({{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}), Ichikishima-hime is often associated with the Buddhist deity [[Benzaiten]], and many shrines dedicated to her are colloquially referred to as Benten (弁才天, 弁財天, or 弁天). She is also frequently enshrined as a subsidiary deity within the precincts of temples and shrines.

According to the myth associated with the descent of the heavenly grandson ({{ill|Tenson kōrin|en|Tenson kōrin|qid=Q1084733|lt=Tenson Kōrin}}), the three goddesses safeguarded Ninigi-no-Mikoto, leading to their veneration as protectors of children and their dedication in child-related shrines.
